classes.purpose: Understand the business question, market, customers, operations, economics, cash, options and planning assumptions
classes.content: The selected model may read the assignment and selected evidence, including company, customer, supplier and personal information when relevant, market evidence, operating and financial data, reviewed assumptions, scenarios, audience and open questions. Both products perform the same business analysis. No automatic anonymization is applied. Company stage and evidence meaning are interpreted by the model and professional, not classified by code.

classes.purpose: Prepare one business analysis using the shared financial model and report compiler
classes.content: Both entry points consume one shared reviewed case and locally run the shared Decimal financial engine. Every selected file is hashed and registered with version, role, review status, audience and confidentiality restrictions. The shared report structure, HTML, JSON and CSV preserve selected file names/relative paths, evidence descriptions, confirmed assumptions and hypotheses, source-figure conflicts and professional decisions, complete calculated figures and IDs, chart lineage, limitations and unresolved matters. This full local audit package is not an automatically bounded model-context projection. The workflow instructs the model to use only the reviewed excerpts, assumptions and calculation records needed for the mandate and allowed for the audience; it does not automatically anonymize content or enforce which local artifacts Codex reads. The compiler itself calls no model or external service. Optional PDF uses a provisioned local Chromium renderer with network requests disabled and only validated HTML. Independent contribution files and legacy cases cannot finalize reports. The model also authors the business recommendation, alternatives, next actions and chart selection. User idea snapshots, provisional interpretations, source-backed external numerical facts and optional commercial price/volume drivers can enter this same context. Pending professional review remains explicit and does not silently discard ordinary interpretation. Supporting workpapers are accessible in a collapsed report appendix; this does not remove them from the HTML file. Explicit presentation data includes report language, source-bound comparison tables, captions, proposed responsible roles and timing, decision criteria, source filenames and versions, page or cell locators, and reference URLs. These fields may enter the selected model context when it authors or reviews the case. URLs are rendered as reader-visible links; the compiler does not fetch them, and PDF rendering blocks network requests. The PDF contains reader-facing source references but hides the technical appendix and expandable workpapers that remain in the HTML. An explicit draft-PDF request can render a partial assessment with a draft label; this does not establish professional approval or remove audience restrictions. Authored comparison groups bind period and scenario labels to existing checked tables. Browser controls only select visibility; all figures and interpretations stay in the report. Shared scales remain fixed across group views. An explicitly requested Sites export retains the same complete HTML and embedded workpapers, and records its exact hash before host-managed publication. Missing inputs in one scenario do not suppress independently complete scenarios; unavailable scenario calculations and dependent claims remain explicit in the report.

classes.purpose: Continue the same business case and assess its proposed financing
classes.content: The selected model may also read the previous registered planning snapshot, the current question, new customer or competitor evidence, changed assumptions, exact input differences, reconsidered conclusions, proposed tests and reopening conditions. Financing assessments may include borrower and existing-debt evidence, proposed lender or investor identity and terms, funding purpose, bank repayment scenarios or equity milestones, cash runway and ownership/return discussion. These are case data, not automatically anonymized. The prior snapshot is hashed and case-bound, and its embedded source restrictions are checked for the new audience. Old case approval cannot silently approve changed inputs. Earlier report folders are preserved; Clara permits revision folders beneath business-plan. The current report contains the cycle and financing reasoning; internal workpapers contain history and exact differences. No lender or investor application is sent by the compiler.

classes.purpose: Assess the provenance and limits of source release and professional review records
classes.content: Declared reviewer identities, timezone-aware review timestamps, rationale, audience-release decisions and exact source hashes can enter model context and are retained in the local case/report package. These are operator-supplied assertions, not authenticated proof of the reviewer or semantic correctness. The compiler does not automatically delete the case, HTML, JSON, CSV or completed PDF. On a caught PDF failure it removes the incomplete PDF while retaining validated non-PDF outputs and an error receipt. Collapsing HTML appendices or hiding them in print does not redact their contents from the HTML.

classes.purpose: Explain a blocked plan without presenting rejected interpretation as a conclusion
classes.content: When calculation contradictions block the plan, submitted narrative and assessment remain in the case record for diagnosis, while accepted narrative is empty and the report withholds the assessment conclusion. Retained source/case contents can still enter Codex context when read; report suppression is not deletion or anonymisation.

boundaries_beyond_codex.destination: Host-provided search services and public market, competitor and financier websites selected for the mandate
boundaries_beyond_codex.purpose: Investigate pricing, demand, competitor developments and actual financing requirements for the current planning question
boundaries_beyond_codex.content: Queries based on public product, market and financier facts; public URLs and relevant retrieved pages or excerpts. The skill prohibits private case documents, unpublished forecasts, interview details and personal identifiers in queries. The compiler itself performs no network research.
controls: A research mandate or explicit route choice is authorization; clarify an optional unchosen route once, not once per query.
Keep research read-only; do not contact customers, competitors, banks or investors or submit applications without explicit authority.
Query selection and compliance with these instructions remain model-led; there is no automatic anonymization or query-content classifier.

boundaries_beyond_codex.destination: OpenAI Sites through the selected host Sites connector
boundaries_beyond_codex.purpose: Publish the validated financial report for the user-selected audience
boundaries_beyond_codex.content: On an explicit Sites route, the host uploads the complete validated report HTML and static Site source to OpenAI Sites, including company information, financial figures, all comparison views, assumptions, source names and relative paths, embedded case workpapers and review records. Hidden or collapsed material remains delivered. Original source files are not separately copied into the public output. Sites manages hosting and visitor access. The helper performs no upload and creates no invitation. Sharing and retention depend on the selected Sites account and service; Vera and Clara do not enforce retention or deletion.
controls: An explicit request to publish through Sites chooses this route; host action-time approval and access checks still apply.
The preparation helper requires a matching report audience, replays the source hashes and report, rejects blocked reports and refuses to overwrite earlier Site candidates.
Only the configured dist output is published. All embedded report data remains included; no automatic anonymization or redaction.
Verify deployment status and intended visitor access. Invitations and messages require authorized recipients; recurring updates require a separate user request.

boundaries_beyond_codex.destination: Python Package Index (PyPI) or the index selected by the user's Python configuration
boundaries_beyond_codex.purpose: Prepare the declared Python dependencies before running a documented workflow CLI
boundaries_beyond_codex.content: Published package requirements and ordinary package-index request metadata. Existing workflow arguments are forwarded to a local Python child; they are not included in the pip install command.
controls: The direct CLI selects published core or registered component requirements before importing workflow modules.
The launcher preserves the working directory and arguments in the local child process; this does not redact arguments or change the workflow data boundary.
An existing matching runtime is reused. Setup installs into a fingerprinted user-scoped environment and propagates failure; it does not install into the case folder.

boundaries_beyond_codex.content: Random installation UUID and opaque capability, Clara/host/runtime versions, platform and workflow technical IDs, failed stage, complete available technical diagnostic chains and measurements, explicit missing-measurement reasons, retry IDs and actual recovery outcomes. No professional helper stdout, client documents, case text, user prompts or arbitrary task logs. Known path, email and credential patterns are removed from technical messages; this mechanical filter does not establish semantic privacy. The host agent must select technical evidence without unrelated personal/client material. The remote channel does not read local files. Saved anonymous connector authorization exchanges a random code with a PKCE verifier, client ID and fixed incident resource; the host saves access/refresh tokens. The server stores token/code hashes, technical callback metadata and a random connection UUID. No personal account signup, user profile, email or client-file permission is involved. Failed helpers retain complete stderr privately on disk; stderr may include unrelated private/client text and is read by the selected host model for semantic review under its existing account. Raw stderr is not forwarded to Mparanza. Only reviewed relevant technical diagnostics, linked by the original report UUID, are submitted as supplemental evidence. Professional stdout is not captured. Installation-preparation failures submit only a fixed technical message, exception type/errno, or the indexed package-relative file name and expected/observed SHA-256 values for a content mismatch. No altered file contents or professional files are read for this report. Managed helpers also send source-bound exception classes, OS error numbers, package-relative stack coordinates, developer-authored error templates and missing required option names automatically. Dynamic exception/argument values, locals, professional stdout and arbitrary source excerpts are not part of these structured events. Process-session UUIDs, persistent operation UUIDs and optional keyed digests of existing run/input-receipt identities bind attempts without disclosing receipt fields or raw client-input hashes. Actual worker interpreter/platform fields are separate from the reporter's interpreter. Capture completeness, pending semantic review, exact remedy/retry events and host verification of the original task remain distinct evidence states; a structured event is not a semantic diagnosis. Current reporting-process version, protocol capabilities and server last-seen time are retained per process session, separately from historical failure versions; they do not establish that all conversations updated. Native-host binding, when invoked, accepts a random host UUID and scoped capability plus an optional explicit native-app label at the same incident service. Only the host capability hash is retained server-side. Stable app-profile UUIDs are derived from host UUID and app label; reporter-instance UUIDs may be task-local and do not count physical computers, plugin copies or people. App grouping grants no additional client status or outcome access. Operator views retain each original report, supplement, outcome and retry event with its actual reporting owner and server receipt time; missing historical task identity is not reconstructed. The native stdio identity bridge verifies its indexed entry, reporter, technical collector and product metadata, then executes an isolated temporary reporter snapshot using existing Python without installing dependencies. Its tool accepts only an existing reporter capability and sends host proof to the fixed register endpoint; it never returns the device key or copies the reporter key into the host identity file. Native broker version/session observations are retained separately from guest reporter and failure-worker observations. When native tools are not exposed in cloud Cowork, the saved remote connector continues to report under its distinct connection identity and physical-host linkage remains unknown; no device controls or folder permissions are expanded automatically. Native-helper failures return source-bound exception classes, errno or HTTP status, package-relative frames and developer-authored templates. Dynamic diagnostic values are not returned; unavailable capture is explicit. This bridge does not return raw stderr or device keys. The central recovery agent may request named technical evidence surfaces through a diagnostic-request remedy. The host AI replies with reviewed technical facts, the original report UUID and request revision. Original-task availability is represented by technical booleans, not task text, client identifiers or file contents. A resume remedy communicates a diagnosed correction to the existing authorized workflow; it does not carry executable code. Technical requests, response UUIDs, applicable revisions and their observed status are retained with the original episode. The central agent may implement and deploy incident-related software fixes through reviewed source and green CI under Fabio’s explicit recovery authorization; it does not receive professional case files or gain user-host permissions. Handled Studio Archive exceptions log their active traceback locally before returning the existing error JSON, allowing the same source-bound collector and host semantic review to retain their actual cause. The operator derives diagnostic publication, exact owner/report/revision receipt and reply states, the existing 15-minute deadline and reporting-owner last service contact from retained records. These delivery facts do not establish physical-host availability, diagnosis or original-task recovery. The operator also projects exact delivery, retry and original-task outcome evidence for all actionable remedy kinds, including software updates. Its 15-minute attention cadence is not an execution timeout. A local alert renderer uses technical incident facts and an AI-reviewed blocker, accountable next action, reason and scheduled check. An optional operator-maintained device label is accepted only with a recorded exact-device verification reference; it is not inferred from the recipient, OS or reporter identity. Rendered operator alerts may include opaque machine/case codes and a verified operator-device label, but no client contents, raw diagnostics, personal identifiers or credentials. The renderer neither sends email nor accesses the registry or client files. It rejects stale followup reviews and cannot assign an unreceived or overdue remedy back to the uncontacted Clara. Recovered labels require matching actual original-task success evidence; incomplete historical bindings remain unknown. The shared API also exposes a separate public workflow-testing endpoint: an allowlisted map of pipeline IDs to testing levels and baseline metadata, without incident details, computer IDs, run IDs or user feedback. Its reset is operator-only and does not change incident records. Native workflow transport supplies the same existing host proof during registration when it is available.
controls: Technical reporting is automatic; stars and optional comment are only the user’s chosen feedback, never inferred from professional context.
The local model-data report stays in the task output; only its hash and opaque receipt link reach the service.
Read the corresponding hosted-service record for exact payload, ownership, retention and recovery boundaries.

boundaries_beyond_codex.purpose: Pipeline usage, outcomes and user satisfaction
boundaries_beyond_codex.content: The existing installation capability authenticates closed-schema events: random run and event UUIDs, sequence, catalog pipeline ID, host, observed product version, timestamps, explicit user/synthetic/agent-test classification and started/resumed/completed/failed/cancelled state. Optional links contain only an existing signed receipt UUID/report digest or an owned incident report UUID. Run ownership, single-run receipt binding and the retained signature are checked server-side. The original stamping service does not attest the identity of the author of a report. The service receives no task text, client identity, filenames, source data, prompt or professional output. Existing connection metadata and rate limiting apply. Saved connector identity is not inferred to be a native computer. Native senders also present the existing anonymous native-computer capability and observed native app when available. The server retains the established computer binding; unlinked guests and standalone OAuth connections remain unlinked. The product field is explicit. Product, run owner and receipt product must match. Baselines and function catalogues are distinct per product. The actual 1–5 integer score, up to 2000 characters of optional user-authored comment, source (chat or form), random event UUID and existing task binding. Nothing is copied automatically from professional context. The host asks once after delivery; no response is unrated. A low score offers one optional question about what failed or was expected. Only catalog pipeline IDs, four testing-level names and counting epoch UUID/time are public. The service privately groups completed runs by proven anonymous computer IDs: the owner-designated computer counts as agent testing, other computers as professional use. Stars, comments, report digests, client documents, task prompts, computer IDs, run IDs and capabilities are not in this response. The owner convention counts computers, not authenticated people; completion does not certify professional correctness. No model call is made by this public projection.
controls: Technical reporting is automatic; stars and optional comment are only the user’s chosen feedback, never inferred from professional context.
The local model-data report stays in the task output; only its hash and opaque receipt link reach the service.
Read the corresponding hosted-service record for exact payload, ownership, retention and recovery boundaries.

boundaries_beyond_codex.content: Unless the user requests --local-only, each substantive run with a durable local report automatically sends exactly schema version, one random per-run receipt UUID, the Clara version when the request was first created, and the SHA-256 digest of the canonical local model-data report, plus ordinary connection metadata. The report itself, workflow and local run IDs, client or case data, professional purpose, phase labels, counts, filenames, file contents, source-document hashes, prompts, and model outputs are not sent. A later verification request sends the same opaque receipt UUID and report digest. Clara and Lucia use receipt schema 2 with the explicit product as a fifth signed request field; legacy Vera schema 1 is preserved.
controls: Technical reporting is automatic; stars and optional comment are only the user’s chosen feedback, never inferred from professional context.
The local model-data report stays in the task output; only its hash and opaque receipt link reach the service.

security_controls.control: The Clara entry point accepts the case only from the selected workspace root, all selected sources inside that workspace, and outputs only in its business-plan directory.

The shared runner verifies the SHA-256 of every selected file, checks input-reference closure, and replays the complete calculated report before export. Altered calculated values or chart data reject compilation.

Every selected source must allow the report audience in intended_audience and confidentiality.allowed_audiences, or have an explicit reviewed audience-release decision bound to its exact SHA-256. Otherwise the compiler rejects all report-package writes. This enforces the declared source restrictions; it does not authenticate the named reviewer or establish that a release was actually authorized.

Calculated financial claims require canonical calculation IDs and exact values. External numerical facts can bind to source-backed evidence IDs with exact values and units. Disagreement blocks readiness; missing inputs or material reviews/conflicts withhold capital recommendations. Ordinary provisional interpretation remains visible. Numeric literals in narrative are rejected. Semantic classification and conclusions remain model-led and subject to professional review.

The optional local Chromium PDF renderer installs a request-abort route before loading the validated generated HTML. Reference URLs remain links; the compiler does not fetch them. This control is limited to that rendering page and does not restrict independent host browsing or connectors.
